description: The Municipality of Livorno publishes complementary geotopographic layers describing building footprints, volumetric units, minor structures, building use, internal and external access, road surfaces, and vehicle, cycling and pedestrian circulation areas. Coverage is the municipality of Livorno. Cadastral building-use and land-consumption annotations are labelled for AI training. The land-consumption lineage specifically records the year a parcel moves from the land cadastre to the building cadastre when construction occurs; it is a building-registration transition, not a direct observation of construction completion. This adds one thematic component to the ten previously identified components. A separately published minor-building entry describes the same class and is retained as a related representation. Four broader archive packages cover buildings and other built structures, roads, the built-stock theme, and mobility/transport. Their class hierarchies overlap the individual layers and do not establish additional disjoint inventories. The transport parent describes graph-based traffic modelling, but unread archive contents do not establish which graph classes are present. No specific simulation method is assigned. Native metadata lists geographic formats and CC BY 4.0. One pedestrian description ends with a vehicle-area label despite its pedestrian body and AC_PED code; that inconsistency remains. Observation dates, geometry accuracy, current service operation and file-use charges are unverified. Native catalogue timestamps describe metadata changes. No archive, feature collection, map or data body was read.

notes: Grouping uses the same native municipal publisher and connected national geotopographic classes for buildings, their access and circulation areas. Component and representation identities remain explicit; a shared host alone does not establish grouping. One pedestrian description ends with a vehicle-area label despite its pedestrian title, body and AC_PED class code; this inconsistency is retained. The native class hierarchy connects these broader packages to the same municipal inventory: Immobili e Antropizzazioni, Strade, Edificato. Their scopes overlap component classes already recorded. The number of disjoint thematic components is not increased by the number of archive packages; archive/feature equivalence is unverified. Fresh Livorno metadata adds the building-registration transition class, a second minor-building publication and the mobility/transport parent package. These add three native member identities, one thematic class and one broader package; representations overlap. Exact earlier Toscana mirror identities remain preserved.
schema_summary: Provider class definitions describe external access points and driveways, road surfaces and adjoining verges, cadastral building-use annotations, building volumetric units, building footprints, vehicle circulation and parking surfaces, minor structures, cycling surfaces, internal building access, pedestrian surfaces. No distribution-file schema or feature rows were read.
